name: BISCA
description: Bisca is Portugal's national trick-taking game, a close cousin of Italian Briscola and Spanish Brisca, sharing the same A-7-K-J-Q ranking. Played with a 40-card Portuguese deck, it features a fixed trump suit revealed by turning a card after the deal, a draw-down-to-empty mechanic, and point-count scoring (61+ out of 120 card points wins). Its elegant simplicity masks rich defensive and offensive play.

content.text: Bisca is Portugal's national trick-taking game, a close cousin of Italian Briscola and Spanish Brisca, sharing the same A-7-K-J-Q ranking. Played with a 40-card Portuguese deck, it features a fixed trump suit revealed by turning a card after the deal, a draw-down-to-empty mechanic, and point-count scoring (61+ out of 120 card points wins). Its elegant simplicity masks rich defensive and offensive play.
Directly descended from the Italian game Briscola, carried to Portugal via trade and cultural exchange. Documented in Portuguese card-game literature from the 18th century onwards.
40 cards: A, 7, K, J, Q, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2 in each suit. Remove 8s, 9s, and 10s from a standard deck.
Deal 3 cards to each player (or more in variants). Turn the next card face-upâ€”this card's suit is Trump. Place the remaining deck crosswise on top of the trump-indicator card.
